configs.description: The PDU as it ships. The 10 ft cord is drawn only as the collar it leaves by. The two bracket sets and the cord retention tray in the box are not drawn.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the data sheet lists "Adjustable Mounting Brackets 2 sets (L-Short, L-Long)" and the user manual (PDF pages 5 to 10) shows a horizontal and a vertical install. No document dimensions an ear, gives its holes' spacing or says where the ears bolt, so only the flush position the photograph shows is named, without a figure.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the PDU with its brackets.

gaps.note: the data sheet's first paragraph says "eight IEC-320 C13, 2 IEC-320 C19 receptacles", ten in all. Its features line, its specification table ("Outlets - Total 8") and the user manual's drawing say six C13 and two C19. The drawing is followed.
gaps.wanted: the maker's word on the count.

gaps.note: a Visio stencil is held for this model (its internal title names a set of PDU products) and was not opened; the faces are drawn from the manual drawing and the photograph.
gaps.wanted: the stencil opened and compared with the faces.

gaps.note: no document shows the top, the bottom or an end of this model. The manual's figures draw the faces only.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top, the bottom and an end, with a scale.

one of `input-dc`, `input-ac` in `attrs.power`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `power` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

banks.note: datasheet - the user manual, PDF page 14: Rear Bank 1 Outlets (callout 5), Rear Bank 2 Outlets (callout 6), Circuit Breaker Bank 1 (7) and Circuit Breaker Bank 2 (8), and the front LED indicators (2). Which breaker feeds which bank is read from the callout names and not shown by a line.

breakers.note: datasheet - "Overload Protection 16 A x 2" (data sheet page 1) and the user manual, PDF page 15, "Circuit Breaker 16 A x 2". The drawing shows each as concentric rings, which is what common/breaker-push-reset@1 draws. That the breakers are push-to-reset is read from the drawing and not stated in a held document.

chassis.note: datasheet - CyberPower PDU30BHVT8R data sheet, page 2: "445 x 44 x 38 mm" (W x H x D) and "17.5 x 1.5 x 1.75 in." (W x D x H) in the user manual, PDF page 15. THE EARS ARE NOT IN IT: the photograph shows an ear at each end outside the body, so 445 is read as the body between the folds. Weight 2.04 kg (data sheet page 2). The finish is black.

front.note: photo-measured - the front photograph, millimetres from the body's left edge and its top: the two lamps centre at 75.2 and 75.0 across, 15.2 and 30.3 down; the maker's name stands at 23.2 to 61.6 across and the model name at 27.3 to 55. The legends BANK 1 and BANK 2 stand beside the lamps, as printed.

input.note: datasheet - "Input Plug Type NEMA L6-30P", "Plug Style Straight (Twist Lock)", "Cord Length (ft.) 10 ft (3.0 m)", derated input current 24 A and maximum 30 A (data sheet page 1). The cord leaves the right end of the rear (callout 9).

method.note: The rear is read off the High Voltage Type rear view in the PDU30BHVT8R user manual (K01-0000512-00), PDF page 14 (printed 13), a straight-on line drawing rendered at 600 dpi. Its body is 1611 px across and 164 px high, 9.82 against the data sheet's 445 by 44, 10.11: 3 percent out, so every position is read at 3.62 px per mm across and 3.73 down and is good to about 1 mm. NO DIMENSIONED DRAWING EXISTS. The front is read off the straight-on photograph on page 1 of the data sheet (body 1763 px by 180 at 300 dpi, 3.96 px per mm across and 4.09 down, aspect within 3 percent) and is good to about 1 mm; its positions are photo-measured.

outlets.note: datasheet - the data sheet, pages 1 and 2: "6 x IEC-320 C13, 2 x IEC-320 C19", "Outlets - Rear 8", "Outlets - Front 0". The prose on page 1 says "eight IEC-320 C13, 2 IEC-320 C19", which makes ten; the features, the table and the drawing say six and two, and are followed (gaps: outlet-count-prose). The drawing numbers no outlet, so the ids run left to right as seen from behind and the unit prints no numbers.

rear.note: drawing - the rear view, millimetres from the body's left edge as seen from behind. The outlets centre at 21.7 down. Left bank (Rear Bank 2, callout 6): C13 at 37.0, 61.3 and 85.6 across, C19 at 132.3. Right bank (Rear Bank 1, callout 5): C13 at 194.5, 218.8 and 244.1, C19 at 295.5. The breaker of Bank 2 (callout 8) is at 335.8 and that of Bank 1 (callout 7) at 360.7, the external site ground (callout 4) at 381.9 and the cord (callout 9) at 411.2. Four small holes (callout 10) stand at 9.9 and 434.9 across, 15.5 and 35.6 down. BANK2 and BANK1 are printed above the left ends of their banks.
